signals.source_text: That’s a wrap on my internship and the start of what’s next. I'm happy to share that I’ll be joining MathWorks full-time this January! Across three projects spanning two product areas, this summer MathWorks gave me an environment where I could bridge my engineering background with my passion for human-centered research and design. I had the opportunity to conduct end-to-end generative research from research plan through hand-off, design and execute usability testing with external users, and explore novel agentic usability evaluations, a process that gave me a much deeper appreciation for integrating AI into the UX processes without losing sight of the people using them. Beyond the work itself, what made this experience so meaningful was the culture. Every door was open for a conversation, and every helping hand was just an ask away. There is a genuine emphasis at MathWorks on giving people the trust and autonomy to tackle problems, and that kind of trust is compounding in nature. When even the interns feel like they can take ownership of the work they do, the work gets better, and that made the decision to return that much easier. A massive thank you to my manager Lynsey Urban , my mentors Shruti Sunil Bhave and Meghna Chatterjee , my sponsors Wen (Michael) Shi, PhD and Adam Cohen , and the entire intern cohort for the guidance, feedback, and support all summer. Looking forward to being back in Boston this January!

signals.source_text: The EV didn't make NVH easier. It pushed the noise higher. Motor whine past 5 kHz. Gear mesh. Inverter harmonics. Road noise now the loudest source in the cabin. The critical band runs 100 Hz to 5 kHz, and no single method covers it. The Engineer's Guide to Modern NVH Simulation shows how to work the full range in MSC Nastran and Actran: heavy-fluid coupling, Virtual SEA, and ODYSSEE ROMs. Preview the first pages, then download the full guide below 👇

signals.author: OceanWings
signals.why_relevant: домены: marine; совпадение с профилем: marine.
signals.source_text: OceanWings and Tsuneishi Shipbuilding complete rigid wingsail retrofit on bulk carrier Maria Topic Ultramax bulk carrier returns to commercial service fitted with a rigid, tiltable wingsail system. --- OceanWings, Tsuneishi Shipbuilding and shipowner Topic have announced the completion of a rigid wingsail installation aboard the Ultramax bulk carrier Maria Topic, with the vessel now returned to commercial service. The retrofit was carried out at Tsuneishi Shipbuilding's facilities in Japan and involved fitting OceanWings' rigid, tiltable wingsail technology to the existing vessel. Topic CEO Alex Albertini commented: "Maria Topic follows Paolo Topic in our journey towards more sustainable shipping. By adding wind-assisted propulsion to an existing bulk carrier, we are continuing to invest in practical technologies that reduce fuel consumption and emissions across our fleet. OceanWings and Tsuneishi Shipbuilding demonstrated a strong understanding of our operational requirements, allowing the retrofit to be completed within the dry dock period." Nakai Toshifumi, Managing Executive Officer and Chief Ship Repair Officer at Tsuneishi Shipbuilding, remarked: "The project demonstrates that wind-assisted propulsion can be efficiently integrated into an existing vessel using Tsuneishi Shipbuilding's ship repair and retrofit expertise, helping accelerate the transition towards more energy-efficient shipping. We are committed to contributing to the industry's decarbonization by leveraging our ship repair and retrofit expertise to bring innovative technologies into practical service." Emmanuel Schalit, CEO of OceanWings, stated: "Maria Topic is the latest proof that our technology is delivering where it matters most: in commercial operation. We designed OceanWings to be simple, robust and adapted to the realities of bulk shipping. This project marks an important industrial milestone for OceanWings, demonstrating our ability to manufacture, deliver and deploy our technology at commercial scale." The Maria Topic retrofit was carried out with support from the EU-funded WHISPER (wind energy harvesting for ship propulsion assistance and power) project, operating under the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under Grant Agreement No. 101096577. The project brings together 13 partners from six European countries to develop and validate modular retrofit solutions combining wind-assisted propulsion and renewable onboard energy systems. Lloyd's Register's involvement in the project is funded by UK Research and Innovation under project agreement number 10065742. OceanWings and Topic are due to share initial operational insights from the vessel at SMM Hamburg in September 2026. #Wind #WindPower #Shipping #Maritime #Japan #France #Italy OceanWings | Tsuneishi Shipbuilding Co., Ltd.
